sheets.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve.
Asset type: production animation sprite atlas for Sona in a local music player.
Image 1 is the EXISTING SONA CHARACTER AND ART STYLE to preserve exactly: tiny chibi girl, short lavender bob, purple eyes, violet over-ear star headphones, dark plum jacket and skirt with mint piping, opaque leggings and purple sneakers, cute detailed softly cel-shaded illustrated sprite. Same face, head/body ratio, costume, line thickness, colors, and gentle polished shading in every single frame. Do not redesign her.
Image 2 is an ANIMATION REFERENCE ONLY: study its sequential poses, grounded feet, clear weight shifts, and coherent motion. Do not copy the green-haired character or simplify Sona to its style.

Re-animate Sona with much better sequential motion, replacing the old isolated poses. Render a transparent PNG atlas, EXACTLY 8 columns by 4 rows (32 full-body sprites). Canvas aspect ratio 2:1. All cells are equal squares, no outer margin, no borders, no labels. Each sprite is centered on its cell; fixed camera, fixed scale: a standing character is 72% cell height, soles on the same baseline at 88% cell height. Preserve generous transparent padding for movement. No floor shadow, aura, particles, sparkle trails, checkerboard, glow halo, or background. Clean transparent alpha. All anatomy and headphones remain inside each cell. Same character size and construction through all rows. Pose changes must be visibly related with intermediate positions, not eight disconnected still images. Hair tips, skirt and jacket have one-frame delayed follow-through.

Read left to right. Each row is ONE cyclic eight-frame animation at evenly spaced times, with frame 8 leading naturally back into frame 1; don't duplicate the first pose at the end.
ROW 1 — relaxed listening/head bob: feet planted. Eight phases of a subtle down-and-up head nod, slight shoulder compression on the downbeat, a brief natural blink in frames 4–5. Hands rest near jacket, warm tiny smile. Head tilt varies only slightly; maintain head size. Usable as calm idle as well.
ROW 2 — two-step: full-body rhythmic left-right step-touch. Frames 1–4 shift weight to her left, close trailing foot and recover; frames 5–8 mirrored right. Hips lower with the weight-bearing knee; arms swing opposite the stepping foot; feet visibly lift and plant. Stable eye expression.
ROW 3 — small joyful jump: frame1 standing prep, 2 bend knees, 3 deepest anticipation crouch, 4 takeoff with arms opening, 5 airborne apex (feet 10% cell height above baseline), 6 descent, 7 soft knee-bent landing, 8 return toward neutral. Character stays same anatomical size; no enlarging while jumping.
ROW 4 — shoulder groove: continuous playful left-right shoulder roll with elbows bent and hands in front at chest height; hands and chest travel in coherent small arcs; knees alternate compression. One upbeat closed-eye smile during the groove. Avoid repeating exactly the same pose.

Priority: crisp beautiful OLD Sona artwork preserved, anatomically coherent clean animation, feet registration and scale stability, readable at 112 px. It is an actual sprite atlas, not a poster or contact sheet with captions.

Use case: identity-preserve. Asset: transparent PNG sprite atlas for existing illustrated chibi girl Sona.
Image 1: original Sona, strict character/style reference. Image 2: our newly made matching dance atlas, strict illustration/scale reference. Image 3: choreography reference ONLY, not its character.
Create a SECOND animation sheet of this EXACT same Sona, never redesign her: short glossy lavender bob, violet eyes, round purple star headphones, dark plum jacket, mint edging, skirt, opaque leggings, purple sneakers, 2.5-head chibi proportions. Preserve fine soft cel shading, polished original artwork, crisp dark contours. Avoid ANY colored fringe, glow or scattered pixels outside her silhouette. All empty space must be pure transparent alpha.

EXACT GRID: 8 columns × 4 rows = 32 full-body sprites, rectangular canvas aspect 2:1; uniform square cells, no labels/grid/borders/background/floor-shadows. Every character fits safely inside its cell. Fixed orthographic camera and fixed body/head scale. Character normally 72% of cell height, head top at 16%, feet baseline at 88%; same vertical baseline across a row except deliberate bent knees. Arms and hair never touch a cell edge. Keep enough transparent margin, no overlapping rows.
Each row is one sequential hand-drawn eight-phase LOOP. Draw useful intermediate poses! Adjacent frames must move along continuous arcs, frame8 approaches frame1. One steady warm smile and open eyes through the whole row, NO repeated winking or rapid expression changes. Hair and skirt follow the direction of motion with delayed overlap.

ROW1 overhead wave: both hands sway overhead toward left in frames1–3, pass through center in4, sway right in5–7, approach center8. Knees softly alternate weight. Wrists and elbows trace smooth continuous arcs, every intermediate hand position between its neighbors.
ROW2 hip sway / hula: hands together in front at waist height trace a horizontal figure-eight, hips shift opposite shoulders, feet planted, left extreme at2, center4, right extreme6, center8. Shoulders counterbalance head. Keep hands visibly attached, no teleporting.
ROW3 windmill arms: playful dance, no acrobatics, feet fixed. One arm circles overhead while the other circles low, exchange roles halfway. Eight equal 45-degree phases, with bent elbows kept anatomically plausible. Same stable smiling front-facing head all8frames. No sudden whole-body rotation.
ROW4 full slow spin: EXACTLY one complete clockwise standing turn, 45-degree increments: front, front-right three-quarter, right profile, back-right three-quarter, back, back-left three-quarter, left profile, front-left three-quarter. Do NOT turn back toward the front before the full circle. Same anatomical scale, anchored feet at baseline, head/body turn together, jacket and skirt flare only slightly. Rear headphones band/hair continuous, same outfit from behind. Frame8 naturally precedes front frame1.

Priority: sequential animation continuity and consistent scale. Art is the old charming Sona style; do not change style or character. Transparent background, no halos, no decorative stars outside the headphones.

Transparent background/clean alpha, no floor shadow, no aura/glow/fringe/sparkles. All hands, hair and feet stay inside their own cell. ROW1 SLEEP LOOP: same Sona seated curled-up on her feet, eyes closed peacefully all eight frames, little hands together tucked against one cheek, headphones retained. One slow inhale/exhale across eight phases, subtle head settling and hair follow-through, same silhouette and small closed-mouth smile throughout. ROW2 CLICK GREETING: one gesture in eight frames. 1 standing smile hands by sides, 2 notice and lift right hand near shoulder, 3 hand reaches cheek level, 4 palm raised and tilted left, 5 palm tilted right, 6 small happy eye smile with palm returning, 7 lower hand, 8 original neutral pose. Feet planted same place, gentle coherent head tilt, left hand stays by jacket. No repeated jump or hand teleport.
ROW3 PICKUP + HELD: 1 neutral standing, 2 shoulders lift slightly and feet relax, 3 startled cute open eyes with hands slightly raised, 4 hanging by an invisible gentle grip at the top of her headphones with feet loosely pointing downward, 5 same hanging pose tiny left dangle, 6 same pose neutral, 7 tiny right dangle, 8 neutral hanging. Arms relaxed at sides, both feet hanging parallel. No visible hand or string. Head and body keep natural proportions; do NOT stretch the anatomy. Maintain a fixed top/headphone anchor for frames4–8, body dangles under it, matching the held row of classic desktop mascots. Small closed happy mouth after initial surprise.
ROW4 DROP / SOFT LANDING: 1 same hanging pose as row3 frame8, 2 feet extend toward ground, 3 toes touch normal floor baseline, 4 knees bend on impact, 5 deepest soft crouch with jacket and hair settling, 6 rise half way, 7 nearly upright, 8 neutral standing matching row2 frame1. Smooth same-size anatomical poses; same ground baseline as dance sheets. Not a jump or random wave.

No props, no arrows, no labels, no additional graphics. Priority consistent identity, coherent sequence and proportions, clean image edges. A professional small game animation atlas, exact 8×4 grid.
